eli: Ran an nsys capture on staging for the fused_flash_v3 path with kv-cache enabled, saw a recurring kv write hotspot around step boundaries. sampling + timeline attached. :eyes:

maya: hmm, what workload / batch/seq?

eli: repro with --batch=8 --seq=2048 using our chat benchmark (deterministic prompts). kernel selector picked flash_attn_fused_kernel but then a huge spike from kv_write_async shows up every ~16ms.

sam: can you paste the nsys command you used?

eli: sure:
```
nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,cublas --output=staging_fusedflash.nsys \
  --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx=stack -- python -m bench.runner --model=redwood/fused_flash_v3 \
  --batch 8 --seq 2048 --kv-cache on
```

eli: perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (timeline view)

jorge: looked at the timeline, two things pop: 1) flash_attn_fused_kernel has a long tail with many short retries (scheduler fragmentation) 2) kv_write_async is serialized by a single stream + host-side memcpy causing backpressure.

maya: that matches a microtrace i dumped — nvprof showed high host-to-device memcpy frequency right before kv writes. paste from logs:
```
[LOG] step 42: kernel flash_attn_fused_kernel duration=3.2ms
[LOG] step 42: kv_write_async queued, host memcpy 0.7ms
[LOG] step 42: stall waiting for memcpy completion 1.4ms
```

sam: interesting — are we choosing flash_attn_fused even when sequence-specific heuristics would prefer tiled_flash? maybe selector thresholds changed in last rollout.

eli: selector config on staging still has heuristic: prefer fused if seq > 1024 and batch <= 16. but the perf model doesn't account for KV write overlap.

jorge: hypothesis: fused variant increases register pressure so kernels finish in bursts and force frequent KV flushes; those flushes are scheduled on the wrong stream (default stream) and serialize with memcpy.

sam: easy check — try run with KV writes pinned to an async stream + cudaMemcpyAsync pinned buffer. also try forcing tiled_flash variant to compare.

eli: i ran two quick experiments: 1) force kernel=tiled_flash -> tail latency dropped 18%, cpu memcpy frequency halved. 2) keep fused but move kv writes -> tail latency down 12%. so both help but different tradeoffs.

maya: can you add those numbers to a short perf note? we'll want to update kernel selector to include a kv-write penalty in the cost model.

eli: short note below (will add to PR):
- workload: chat-bench batch=8 seq=2048
- baseline: fused_flash_v3, kv on default stream -> p99 latency = 42.3ms, observed kv-write stalls ~1.2ms every 16ms
- tiled forced: p99 = 34.8ms (-17.8%)
- fused + async-kv-stream: p99 = 37.3ms (-11.8%)
- nvprof/nsys artifacts: /tmp/staging_fusedflash.nsys, perfetto trace at https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123

perf-bot: Automated note: uploaded nsys bundle to s3://redwood-perf/staging/2387654321/staging_fusedflash.nsys :white_check_mark:

sam: nice, next steps: (1) add kv-write overlap feature to selector cost model, (2) add a small experiment in CI that asserts no >10% p99 regression when toggling fused vs tiled for seq>=1024, (3) fix default kv write stream in runtime to use async pool.

jorge: i'll own (3) and a quick unit-test for stream assignment. eli can you draft the selector change and a perf-test?

eli: will do, opening draft PR with traces and numbers. tagging @sam for priority. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — this explains the regression we saw in last deploy. good catch.

sam: great thread. keep traces and small reproducer in PR so we can run on CI infra.

eli: done, PR up at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 (draft). includes perf note and nsys artifacts.

perf-bot: CI perf regression check: queued for run on perf-cluster-2.

eli: closing the loop once CI finishes. thanks all. :rocket:
